Article Title: Dasgaja from the sky: Why India and Nepal are deploying drones over no-man’s land
Article Text:
Maintaining the Dasgaja buffer remains a challenge. Photo credit: ANI

What is Dasgaja?

Why India and Nepal are turning to drones to map a border where markers, rivers and land use have complicated boundary management.

An open but defined border

Cross-border occupation

What happens when a river moves but the border doesn't?

Missing boundary pillars and shifting river courses can make an already complex frontier harder to identify on the ground.

Most of the border is mapped

Why are boundary pillars a problem?

India and Nepal are using drone technology to survey parts of their open border where physical markers and changing landscapes create uncertainty.

Why use drones now?

Is this related to Kalapani and Lipulekh?

What this drone survey really means

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India and Nepal are turning to drones to map a stretch of their border that, on paper, is supposed to remain empty.The area is known as Dasgaja, the no-man's-land or buffer zone along the India-Nepal boundary. But on the ground, parts of it have been cultivated, occupied or built upon. Rivers have changed course, while thousands of boundary pillars have gone missing or been damaged.Now, the two countries want to map that mismatch from the air.At the 13th meeting of the Survey Officials' Committee in Lucknow this month, India and Nepal agreed to use unmanned aerial vehicles to map cross-border occupation, including encroachments in Dasgaja. The joint survey is expected to begin after the monsoon, around September or October, and be completed within three years.The two sides will then jointly analyse the aerial imagery to establish how much land is being used by citizens on the other side of the recognised boundary.The move follows remarks by Nepal prime minister Balendra Shah in Parliament in May that India had encroached on Nepali land and that Nepal, too, had occupied Indian land in some places.Nepal's foreign ministry later clarified that Shah was referring to cross-border occupation and encroachment in Dasgaja, rather than making a new territorial claim against India.Dasgaja literally means "ten yards". It refers to the no-man's-land or buffer zone along the India-Nepal boundary.There is some variation in how its width is described. Indian reports generally refer to a 10-yard no-man's-land, while a study by Nepal's Institute of Foreign Affairs describes a 20-yard-wide buffer, with 10 yards extending from the boundary on either side.The principle is straightforward: the immediate area around the international boundary should remain free of occupation, making the border easier to identify, inspect and maintain.In practice, that is difficult along an open border stretching about 1,880 km. The boundary runs through farmland, settlements, forests, roads and river systems, while communities on both sides maintain deep social and economic links.Nepal's Institute of Foreign Affairs has documented people living in makeshift houses and tents within Dasgaja. Even when security forces remove such settlements, people can return.So, while Dasgaja is meant to function as a buffer on paper, parts of it have gradually become intertwined with everyday life and livelihoods along the border.India and Nepal share an open border. There is no continuous fence separating the two countries, and people routinely cross it for work, trade, family and other activities.An open border, however, does not mean an undefined border.The international boundary is established through boundary pillars, maps and geographic coordinates. Dasgaja provides an additional buffer around that line.Maintaining the physical markers has become a persistent challenge.According to Nepal's Department of Survey, 8,554 boundary pillars were installed along the border. Of these, 1,325 are missing and 1,956 are partially or completely damaged.A missing pillar does not automatically alter the international boundary. Its location can be reconstructed using survey records, coordinates and maps. But on the ground, the absence of a marker can make it far harder to establish where the boundary runs, particularly where fields, houses and roads are close to the line.The drone survey goes beyond Dasgaja. India and Nepal also want to map what officials describe as cross-border occupation.These are instances in which citizens of one country live on, cultivate or otherwise use land that falls on the other side of the legally recognised boundary.Nepal's foreign ministry said this was the issue Shah was referring to when he spoke about Nepal occupying Indian territory. It specifically linked the problem to the Fixed Boundary Principle used in riverine sections of the border.Several sections of the India-Nepal boundary run through or alongside rivers. Rivers naturally shift course through erosion, sediment deposition and the formation of new channels.That can create complicated situations when the legal boundary is tied to a position established in earlier surveys.Under the Fixed Boundary Principle, the boundary can remain fixed even when the river around it changes course.The result can be highly unusual: a farmer may continue cultivating land that a family has used for generations, only for a later survey to establish that the land now lies on the other side of the international boundary.Nepal's foreign ministry identified such riverine changes as one reason for cross-border occupation. Nepal's Kantipur has reported that decades of river-course changes have shifted thousands of hectares of land from one side of the border to the other.The new drone survey is not an attempt to redraw or rediscover the India-Nepal boundary.Technical boundary work dates back to 1981, when the Joint Technical Level Nepal-India Boundary Committee was established.After years of surveying, the committee prepared 182 strip maps covering about 98 per cent of the boundary. The maps were finalised in 2007 and excluded the unresolved areas of Kalapani and Susta.India's ministry of external affairs has also recorded that the strip maps covering 98 per cent of the boundary were authenticated in 2007.But the maps were never formally ratified by both countries as a final settlement.Nepal maintained that outstanding disputes had to be resolved, while India sought their endorsement.Even so, they remain an important technical reference.A boundary line on a map can be difficult to identify in a field without a physical marker.That is why India and Nepal maintain thousands of boundary pillars along the frontier. But many have been damaged, destroyed or lost, particularly in areas affected by rivers and erosion.The two countries have been working to restore them. At the seventh meeting of the Boundary Working Group in July 2025, India and Nepal agreed to jointly construct new pillars and repair damaged ones as part of their technical boundary work.Established in 2014, the Boundary Working Group deals with issues including the clearing of no-man's-land, construction and maintenance of boundary pillars, updating cross-border property records and other technical border matters.It does not cover the unresolved Kalapani and Susta disputes.The technical mechanism operates at three levels: the Boundary Working Group, the Survey Officials' Committee and Joint Field Survey Teams. Field teams conduct ground surveys, while the SOC and BWG examine the findings and determine the next technical steps.The immediate objective is simple: get a far more precise picture of what is happening on the ground.The UAVs will capture aerial images of areas where cross-border occupation is suspected. Indian and Nepali officials will then analyse the imagery jointly and compare it with existing maps, coordinates, boundary pillars and field records.Aerial imagery can show precisely where fields, houses, roads, rivers and other physical features sit in relation to the established boundary.But the most important element is not the drone. It is the joint verification.If both countries work from the same imagery and agree on the technical facts of a particular location, it becomes easier to determine what needs to happen next.The jointly verified record could eventually provide a basis for negotiating the removal of encroachments, restoration of land or, where necessary, compensation.The India-Nepal border has several separate disputes.Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura concern Nepal's territorial claims in the western sector and competing interpretations of historical maps, documents and the course of the Kali or Mahakali River.Susta is another separate dispute involving changes in the course of the Gandak or Narayani River.The current technical mechanism does not cover these unresolved areas. The 2025 BWG agreement specifically kept Susta and Kalapani-Lipulekh-Limpiyadhura outside its technical work.The Dasgaja exercise is narrower. It deals with no-man's-land, boundary infrastructure and cross-border occupation along the established boundary.At first glance, sending drones over Dasgaja may look like a relatively routine surveying exercise. It is anything but.The India-Nepal border is unusual: open to people, but fixed in law; socially intertwined, but internationally sovereign. Over decades, rivers have shifted, settlements have expanded, farms have crossed invisible lines and boundary markers have disappeared.That has created a gap between the border that exists on maps and the border experienced on the ground.The drones are an attempt to close that gap with evidence.They will not settle Kalapani. They will not redraw the map. And they will not, by themselves, resolve every dispute over land.But they could give India and Nepal something that has often been missing in sensitive border discussions: a shared, current and verifiable picture of what is actually happening on the ground.
Article Summary: India and Nepal are using drone technology to survey parts of their open border. The area is known as Dasgaja, the no-man's-land or buffer zone along the India- Nepal boundary. But on the ground, parts of it have been cultivated, occupied or built upon. Rivers have changed course, while thousands of boundary pillars have gone missing.

Article Title: India vs China: How their nuclear-capable missile arsenals compare
Article Text:
The Agni family of missiles are designed to carry the weight of India's strategic weapons. (Image credit: DRDO)

Indian and Chinese strategic missiles

China and India, Asia's two most powerful countries, have spent decades building ballistic missile arsenals. These ballistic missiles are strategic weapons that act as a deterrent, under the concept of Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD). This prohibitive concept states that two nuclear armed powers will not use these weapons on each other, as the use of such a weapon will ensure a retaliatory strike, thereby increasing the cost for the attacker. India and China's strategic missile arsenals now bear resemblance, but also at the same time there are differences in capability. The two countries also are also employing different philosophies for the use of these weapons, as the US Naval Institute states that China is building a significant amount of missile capability to hit US bases in the vast Pacific.While India is building its strategic missile arsenal to act as an insurance against attacks from nuclear weapons armed entities. This concept is enshrined in India's no first use policy for nuclear weapons. India depends on the Agni family of missiles for its land based nuclear deterrence, while China depends on the Dongfeng series.At the shorter end of the spectrum, China's road-mobile DF-16 offers a range between 800 and 1,000 kilometres, giving it reach over Taiwan and much of the western Pacific.India's comparable system, the Agni-I, delivers a range of 700 to 900 kilometres, and while it lacks the DF-16's higher payload capacity of up to 1,500 kilograms, it remains a reliable, road and rail-mobile system tailored specifically for shorter-range contingencies closer to India's borders.Moving up the ladder in terms of range and capability, China's DF-21, one of the People's Liberation Army's most storied missiles, offers a range of up to 2,500 kilometres and famously spawned the world's first anti-ship ballistic missile variant, the DF-21D. India's Agni-II sits in a similar bracket, with a declared range of 2,000 to 3,500 kilometres, and has long been described as central to India's deterrence posture with respect to China, despite New Delhi's insistence that its missile programme is not aimed at any single adversary.At the intermediate range, China's DF-26, capable of striking targets over 5,000 kilometres away, including American bases in Guam, sits close in class to India's Agni-III, which offers a declared range of 3,000 to 5,000 kilometres and has been noted for a circular error probable of just around 40 metres, making it among the most accurate missiles in its class. This accuracy allows India to rely on smaller-yield warheads while still achieving high lethality, a design philosophy that keeps the system relatively compact for its range class.Where the comparison becomes genuinely interesting is at the intercontinental tier. China's DF-31A, a solid-fuel ICBM, boasts a range in excess of 11,000 kilometres. India's Agni-V, its first genuine intercontinental system, offers a declared range of 7,000 to 8,000 kilometres, though some Chinese analysts have suggested its true reach may extend closer to 8,000 kilometres once payload adjustments are factored in. Both missiles share canisterised, road-mobile configurations, a design choice that improves survivability and reduces launch preparation time.At the very top sits China's DF-41, believed to carry ten to twelve MIRV warheads across a range of 12,000 to 15,000 kilometres, making it one of the longest-range missiles in the world. India's answer, the still-developing Agni-VI, is expected to offer a comparable range of as much as 10,000 kilometres, with reports suggesting it could eventually be fitted with MIRV warheads and even a submarine-launched variant, mirroring China's own efforts to build a survivable, multi-domain nuclear triad.Taken together, the comparison suggests India has broadly kept pace with China across most range categories, even as Beijing continues to hold an edge in payload flexibility, warhead multiplicity, and the sheer scale of its overall missile inventory.
Article Summary: India and China have spent decades building ballistic missile arsenals. These ballistic missiles are strategic weapons that act as a deterrent. China is building a significant amount of missile capability to hit US bases in the Pacific. India is building its strategic missile arsenal to act as an insurance against attacks from nuclear weapons armed entities.

Article Title: How is Gisele Bündchen richer than Tom Brady despite not working for 11 years? The business empire behind her extraordinary fortune

Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen (Image via Getty Images)

Gisele Bündchen’s modeling career built a huge fortune

Tom Brady’s net worth comes from football and business

10-year, $375 million deal with Fox Sports

It is how consistently Bündchen’s fashion career generated money on a global scale.Gisele Bündchen entered modeling as a teenager and turned a traditional fashion career into a worldwide business. She became the world’s highest-paid model for much of the period from 2002 through 2017, according to Forbes-linked reporting.Her earnings did not depend on runway appearances alone. Major campaigns, beauty contracts, fragrances and brand partnerships helped transform her fame into long-term income. Forbes reported that Bündchen earned about $30.5 million in 2016, with deals involving brands such as Chanel and Carolina Herrera, alongside her own business ventures.Her career earnings were remarkable even before she stepped away from regular runway work. Forbes estimated in 2014 that she had earned $386 million from modeling since 2001.That helps explain the wealth gap. His biggest financial engine was his 23-year NFL career, during which he collected substantial playing salaries and bonuses. Article Title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay flags off 250 new buses, including 130 electric buses
Article Text:
Chief Minister S. Joseph Vijay flags off new buses at St George Fort in Chennai on Tuesday.

(With Agency Inputs)





CHENNAI: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday inaugurated new bus services operated by the Metropolitan Transport Corporation (MTC) and Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporations at the Secretariat.He flagged off 130 low-floor electric buses worth Rs 234.5 crore and 120 other buses worth Rs 55.8 crore for public use.The 130 EV buses are from Switch Mobility, a subsidiary of Ashok Leyland and are part of Tamil Nadu’s broader green mobility programme.The CM boarded one of the buses and inspected its amenities.Earlier on Monday, CM Vijay announced the expansion of the fare-free bus travel scheme for women, making services such as deluxe and express buses free for beneficiaries.Making several announcements in the Assembly, Vijay, fulfilling TVK's key electoral assurances, announced three free cooking gas cylinders and also declared that the Parandur greenfield airport project will be shelved.The project had been strongly opposed by farmers who did not wish to part with their farm lands."There will be no riders like income ceiling or number of trips for women to avail fare-free bus travel - Vettri Payanam," Vijay said, making a statement under Rule 110.Women can also travel free of charge on Express, LSS and Deluxe government buses operating in metropolitan and urban areas, as well as on regular fare buses in suburban (Mofussil) and hilly areas.The scheme will be rolled out on October 2, coinciding with Gandhi Jayanthi. Vijay said the move will entail an additional expenditure of Rs 6,000 crore per annum for the state government.On the Annapoorani Super Six scheme, a major welfare promise made by Vijay in the run-up to the April Assembly election, assuring six free LPG cylinders to every eligible family in Tamil Nadu every year to reduce household living expenses, the Chief Minister said three free cooking gas cylinders will initially be provided, with the amount credited directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries."This will reduce the burden of the people who have been spending extra amount to obtain the cylinders. The government has decided to provide the cost of the cooking gas cylinders. Three free LPG cylinders will be given in the first phase and the price for cylinders will be directly credited into the bank accounts of the beneficiaries," Vijay said, amidst loud thumping of tables by the Treasury.The move will benefit 1,30,16,104 families with an annual income of nearly Rs 2.5 lakh, economically backward families, small and medium farmers, differently abled people and poor families."The preparatory work has commenced and the scheme will be launched this Pongal (mid-January) 2027 festival," Vijay said and added the state government will allocate Rs 4,000 crore per annum for this initiative.
Article Summary: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday inaugurated new bus services operated by the Metropolitan Transport Corporation (MTC) and Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporations at the Secretariat. He flagged off 130 low-floor electric buses worth Rs 234.5 crore and 120 other buses worth £ 55.8 crore for public use.

Article Title: Karnataka SIR: 4.02 crore voters set for final rolls, 43.81 lakh face notices
Article Text:
Karnataka is revising its electoral rolls on a large scale (Representative image)

How the notice phase will work :





BENGALURU: As the state moved to the next phase of special intensive revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls, Monday, with the claims and notice period, draft SIR rolls already had 1.07 cr of Karnataka’s 5.5 cr voters axed as they were on the ASDDO category.That number was frozen on Aug 17 night. Now, the election commission will now work with just 4.4 cr voters who are on the draft rolls. Of these, at least 4.02 crore will make it to the final list of Oct 27 as they are not due for notices.Of the 4.4 cr voters on the draft list, the remainder 43.81 lakh voters are due to receive notices and have to furnish documents, and upon verification, they too can be added to the final rolls that will be published Oct 27.Bengaluru emerged as the biggest hotspot for SIR voter verification as 46.88 lakh of its 1.03 cr voters left out of the draft rolls. And from 56.99 lakh who made it to the draft rolls, 24 lakh face notices.Booth level officers (BLOs) will deliver the notices over the next two months. These cover voters who either did not map themselves to the 2002 electoral data or whose mapping threw up one of nine logical discrepancies identified by the chief electoral officer’s (CEO) office.All such voters will be listed at their respective polling stations, CEO Anbu Kumar told reporters.A voter who receives a notice will have to produce at least one document from the list of 11 printed on the reverse of the enumeration form.The electoral registration officer (ERO) can seek up to three documents, including Aadhaar, and the BLO will upload these during the visit. “But no specific document will be sought right now, it will be a general uploading of documents,” a CEO office official said, adding that the ERO retains discretion to seek a particular document.The notice will specify the date, time and venue of the hearing, which the voter must attend in person; there is no provision for a virtual hearing. Voters who are ill or unable to travel can have the ERO or assistant ERO conduct verification at their homes.A voter who misses the hearing can be given another opportunity at the ERO’s discretion.Officials said hearing venues would generally be close to voters’ homes, and the number of polling booths has been increased so that no voter is more than 2km from where they cast their vote.Once documents are verified, the ERO will issue a speaking order if satisfied with the claim, potentially as early as the following day via the BLO.If a claim is rejected, the ERO must record the reasons in a speaking order, to be delivered by the BLO.Voters whose claims are rejected can appeal to the district election officer, who is also the deputy commissioner, and if unresolved, take the matter up with CEO Anbu Kumar in a second appeal.
Article Summary: Karnataka is revising its electoral rolls on a large scale. Of the 4.4 cr voters on the draft list, the remainder 43.81 lakh voters are due to receive notices and have to furnish documents. Upon verification, they too can be added to the final rolls that will be published Oct 27.

Article Title: ED raids 8 locations in fake call centre case, Mohali premises linked to fraud
Article Text:
The Enforcement Directorate conducted searches at eight locations across India.





MOHALI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has conducted searches at eight locations in connection with a suspected fake call centre fraud and money laundering case, with sources indicating that a key premises linked to the alleged operation was located in Sector 108, Mohali.According to sources, the ED's Chandigarh Zonal Office carried out searches at premises associated with Vijay Raj Kapuria, Varinder Raj, M/s Infimum Enterprises LLP and other persons and entities allegedly linked to the case. The searches covered locations in Chandigarh, Mohali and Madhya Pradesh.Sources said the agency recovered around Rs 20 lakh in cash, besides digital devices and other material during the searches. The action was part of an investigation into an alleged fraud targeting foreign nationals through a fake call centre.Mohali Premises Under InvestigationSources said the ED case stems from an FIR registered at Sohana police station in Mohali and the subsequent charge sheet filed by the Punjab Police.According to the investigation, an alleged illegal call centre was being operated from Emaar, Plot No. 29, Sector 108, Mohali.The operation allegedly targeted foreign nationals and generated proceeds through fraudulent means.Money Routed Through Multiple ChannelsSources said the investigation found that the alleged fraud proceeds were transferred through PayPal, Stripe, banking channels, Bitcoin and other cryptocurrency transactions, besides hawala channels.The funds were allegedly subsequently routed to accounts linked to fake or shell companies based in the US, making it difficult to trace the ultimate beneficiaries.The investigation also revealed, according to sources, that the bank account of M/s Infimum Enterprise LLP received funds directly from several suspicious foreign entities allegedly used as shell companies.The ED is now examining the financial trail, digital evidence and transactions to identify the beneficiaries and determine the extent of the alleged money laundering network.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate conducted searches at eight locations across India. The searches covered locations in Chandigarh, Mohali and Madhya Pradesh. The action was part of an investigation into an alleged fraud targeting foreign nationals through a fake call centre. Money was allegedly transferred through PayPal, Stripe, banking channels, Bitcoin and other cryptocurrency transactions.

Article Title: Who is Gautam Rangarajan? Indian-origin strategist appointed to key role by UK PM Andy Burnham
Article Text:
Indian-origin strategist Gautam Rangarajan.

Who is Gautam Rangarajan ?

What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. However, the UK PM's office said his appointment draws on his experience in corporate strategy and transformation.His role comes as Burnham undertakes a broader restructuring of the machinery of government, including the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.Rangarajan is expected to play a role in the planned transformation at the heart of the British government.Away from strategy and public service, Rangarajan also has a creative side. He describes himself as a professional choral singer and music producer, alongside his work in corporate strategy and organisational transformation.The appointment comes as Burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of Labour Party leader and Prime Minister.His administration has announced structural changes, including the launch of No. 10 North in Manchester and the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.While the full scope of Rangarajan's new role remains unclear, his appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.
Article Summary: Gautam Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive. He has more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting. His appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.

Article Title: In 2020, Minnesota funded a $1.918 million Shell Rock River habitat program; by 2025, it had protected or restored 588 acres
Article Text:
Shell Rock River Watershed District (Image Credit: www.shellrock.org)

A habitat program takes shape

Three properties protected

Wetlands and prairie restored

More acres than planned

A longer-term conservation effort

In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. According to a 2025 final report from the Lessard-Sams Outdoor Heritage Council, the program ultimately protected, restored or enhanced 588 acres of habitat in the Shell Rock River watershed, exceeding its original goal of 483 acres.The funding was provided under Minnesota Laws 2020, with the appropriation directed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources for an agreement with the Shell Rock River Watershed District. The funding was intended to support land acquisition as well as the restoration and enhancement of aquatic habitat within the watershed. The program focused on several types of conservation work, including acquiring properties, restoring wetlands and improving aquatic habitat. The projects were selected using conservation planning and monitoring intended to identify areas where habitat improvements could provide significant benefits.The Shell Rock River Watershed is a shallow-lake system that supports fish, waterfowl and other wildlife. According to the final report, restoration projects were targeted at addressing habitat degradation and improving conditions for native fish, waterfowl and wildlife.One part of Phase IX involved acquiring three properties: the Glenville Property, the Bancroft Property, and the Church Lake Property. The District closed on the Glenville Property in March 2021 and the Bancroft Property in September 2021. For the Church Lake Property, the District transferred the deed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources in December 2024 after acquiring and restoring the parcel.The final report says these acquisitions contributed to the program's permanent protection of 218 acres. Another 370 acres of habitat and wetlands were enhanced or restored through the program. Together, those accomplishments contributed to the reported total of 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.The program included several restoration projects beyond property acquisition. The Bancroft Wetland Restoration was initiated in 2020, with construction beginning in June 2024 and largely completed by the fall of that year. Additional seeding work was completed in spring 2025. Another project focused on Panicum Prairie, where habitat enhancement work was carried out across 300 acres. The project involved native prairie vegetation and was substantially completed in February 2025, with final work completed in May.The program also supported the Fountain Lake In-Lake Habitat Project. Work included additional rock reefs and rock boulder clusters intended to improve fish habitat. The report notes that Phase IX funds were used to expand the scope of this work after the District determined additional funds were available. These projects addressed different parts of the watershed's ecosystem, from wetlands and prairie habitat to aquatic areas. The broader aim was to improve habitat conditions while protecting areas that could provide long-term benefits for wildlife.The program's original accomplishment plan called for 483 acres. By the end of the project, the final total had reached 588 acres, 105 acres more than initially planned. The report attributes the increase to the addition of the In-Lake Habitat Project and the Church Lake Property to Phase IX.According to the report, all grant funds were spent. The final grant expenditure remained $1.918 million, while the program's final total including leverage was $1.9479 million.The work is intended to continue beyond the end of the grant. The Shell Rock River Watershed District relies on multiple funding sources, including a local option sales tax, local levy and public funding, to maintain conservation projects. The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources will also maintain the Church Lake Property, which it owns.The program's results illustrate how a single state-funded conservation effort can combine land protection, wetland restoration, prairie enhancement and aquatic habitat improvements. Rather than focusing on one habitat type, Phase IX combined several projects across the Shell Rock River watershed. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored. The completed work represents a combination of permanent land protection and habitat improvements designed to support Minnesota's fish, waterfowl and wildlife over the long term.
Article Summary: In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.

Article Title: After CEO Marc Benioff told everyone to stop getting worried, Salesforce does what it has never done before with its 'name'
Article Text:
When Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff said that stop worrying about SaaSpocalypse

Just months after the Salesforce CEO told everyone to stop getting anxious about AI taking away software jobs, the company has joined hands with one of the biggest AI companies to do what it has never done before. Salesforce and Anthropic expanded their strategic partnership and unveiled 'Claudeforce', a new way for salespeople to work within Anthropic’s product. The announcement marks the first time that Salesforce has ever added its "Force" suffix at the end of another company's product.Claudeforce is launching as a plugin with 37 pre-built sales skills that will allow Claude users to compose emails, update records and take other relevant actions, according to a release. The companies said they plan to introduce more integrations across Claude, Salesforce and its messaging platform Slack in the future.“By fusing Claude’s extraordinary reasoning with the trusted data, workflows, and governance every enterprise runs on, we’re delivering a dynamic interface that thinks, reasons, and acts,” Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff said in a statement. “This is how every business will run.”In February this year, Salesforce pulled out all the stops to convince investors that the AI revolution won’t be its death when it announced fourth-quarter earnings. The huge clarification came as the Software-as-a-service (SaaS) stocks, with Salesforce as their poster child, continued to get hammered lately. Fearing that the rise of AI agents will undermine software companies, making their per-employee-seat business models obsolete, investors have been running away from them. The situation has been dubbed the “SaaSpocalypse.” The concept reportedly hung so heavily in the air during the earnings call that CEO Marc Benioff mentioned the term at least six times.“You’ve heard about the SaaSpocalypse? And it isn’t our first. We’ve had a few of them,” he said, later adding, “If there is a SaaSpocalypse, it may be eaten by the Sasquatch because there are a lot of companies using a lot of SaaS because it just got better with agents.”“Through this partnership, companies can point Claude at the customer information and business context that they’ve been building in Salesforce for decades — surfacing the insights that really matter and helping their businesses run more efficiently and grow more quickly,” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in a statement.All in all, Salesforce and its software peers have been under pressure as investors question whether AI tools from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI will replace them. Salesforce shares are down about 22% this year after dropping 20% in 2025. The Nasdaq, meanwhile, is up about 35% since the end of 2024.
Article Summary: Salesforce and Anthropic have unveiled 'Claudeforce', a new way for salespeople to work within Anthropic’s product. The announcement marks the first time that Salesforce has ever added its "Force" suffix at the end of another company's product.

Article Title: Satya Nadella recently shared a rare data point, said that annual revenue of Microsoft's Cloud computing division topped $100 billion; but why it left some analysts 'unhappy'
Article Text:
Satya Nadella

What Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella revealed about company’s cloud business

‘Capital spending numbers don't add up cleanly’

Why Azure's hidden numbers matter so much

Microsoft’s cloud business recently crossed a major milestone, but the company still isn’t telling investors the full story, a report has said. CEO Satya Nadella revealed on an earnings call that Azure’s annual revenue has topped $100 billion for the first time – which is a rare disclosure from a company that has long kept its cloud numbers under wraps. Yet even this headline figure hasn’t been enough to satisfy analysts, who reportedly say Microsoft's financial reporting remains far less transparent than its biggest rivals. Across three key pillars shaping the company’s AI future, its cloud business, its capital spending and its ties with OpenAI, Microsoft's disclosures fall noticeably short of what shareholders would ideally want to see, as per a report by The Wall Street Journal.In its most recent annual report, Microsoft simply stated that “Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 41%” for the fiscal year ending June 30. Notably absent were the actual dollar figures, comparison numbers from the previous year, and any breakdown of expenses or profits tied specifically to Azure. During Microsoft’s July earnings call, Nadella did offer one unusual nugget, revealing that Azure's annual revenue had crossed the $100 billion mark.Instead of breaking Azure out on its own, Microsoft folds it into a broader category called “Intelligent Cloud,” which also includes older legacy software products. This leaves investors guessing where the legacy revenue stops and Azure’s actual growth begins. Compare this to Amazon, which reports Amazon Web Services, the largest cloud provider globally, as its own separate segment complete with sales figures, expenses, and margins. Azure ranks second in the cloud market, yet its financial details remain largely hidden from public view.Microsoft’s cash-flow statement showed $115.9 billion spent on property and equipment last year, a figure the company itself used to calculate free cash flow. However, in a separate release, the company reported total capital expenditure of $145.3 billion, a number that included assets acquired through finance leases. While Microsoft does share separate figures for finance leases, simply adding them to the property and equipment spending doesn't actually match the $145.3 billion total, and the company hasn't offered any explanation reconciling the difference.This lack of segment-level clarity carries the biggest consequences for investors trying to understand where Microsoft's money is actually going. Most of the company’s massive capital spending is being funnelled into Azure, the platform running on an enormous web of data centers that powers much of today’s internet and fuels many AI models.By burying Azure inside the broader Intelligent Cloud segment, Microsoft effectively conceals the true margins, costs and capital intensity behind its AI expansion. This blending mixes an expensive AI infrastructure business with a separate, high-margin software business, making it impossible to see how profitable Azure actually is on its own.Intelligent Cloud is one of Microsoft's three operating segments and accounted for 42% of total sales last year. Its revenue climbed 30% to roughly $138 billion, while the cost of that revenue rose even faster at 44%, reaching $58 billion. Operating expenses grew 7% to $23 billion, leaving operating income at about $57 billion, up 28% from the year before.Somewhere buried within these combined figures sits Azure's actual performance, numbers Microsoft has chosen not to disclose separately. Yet oddly, the company provides far more detailed breakdowns for much smaller businesses, like Xbox and LinkedIn, which brought in about $22 billion and $20 billion respectively last year.
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella revealed on an earnings call that Azure’s annual revenue has topped $100 billion for the first time. Yet even this headline figure hasn’t been enough to satisfy analysts, who reportedly say Microsoft's financial reporting remains far less transparent than its biggest rivals.

Article Title: Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion in AI deal
Article Text:
Nvidia employees have reportedly seen their wealth rise sharply

Why Hugging Face matters to Nvidia's strategy

A price tag far outpacing revenue

Nvidia's broader bet on AI demand

The deal follows a recent security scare

Nvidia has reportedly agreed to buy the open‑source AI model repository Hugging Face for $12.9 billion according to The Information. This deal would mark one of Nvidia’s biggest acquisitions to date and also underscores CEO Jensen Huang’s bet that demand for AI technology is still expanding rather than peaking. For those unaware, Hugging Face hosts open‑source large language models and datasets, giving Nvidia a powerful position at a time when rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI are exploring their own chip alternatives to Nvidia’s GPUs. The reported price tag stands in sharp contrast to Hugging Face’s annualised revenue of $150 million.Acquiring Hugging Face would give Nvidia control over one of the most important hosting platforms for open-source large language models and datasets, at a moment when builders of closed-source models — including Anthropic and OpenAI — are working to develop their own custom chips as alternatives to Nvidia's graphics processing units. Owning Hugging Face would give Nvidia a foothold deeper into the open-source side of the AI ecosystem, an area increasingly important as competition over chip dependency intensifies.The reported $12.9 billion price stands in sharp contrast to Hugging Face's annualised revenue, which The Information reported earlier this week at just $150 million underscoring how much of the valuation is built on strategic and growth expectations rather than current earnings.Neither Nvidia nor New York-based Hugging Face immediately responded to Reuters' requests for comment outside of regular business hours.The Hugging Face report emerged the same day Nvidia forecast a 70% jump in revenue for its next fiscal year, reinforcing the company's confidence that AI demand remains on a steep upward trajectory. Nvidia also disclosed that it has $18 billion committed to equity investments through fiscal year 2027, part of its continued strategy of embedding itself financially across the AI industry rather than relying solely on chip sales.The acquisition report also comes about a month after Hugging Face was hit by a security incident in which an OpenAI model reportedly went rogue and triggered a hack that compromised Hugging Face's infrastructure — an episode that raised fresh questions about security risks tied to hosting and running third-party AI models at scale.
Article Summary: Hugging Face hosts open‑source large language models and datasets, giving Nvidia a powerful position at a time when rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI are exploring their own chip alternatives to Nvidia’s GPUs. The reported $12.9 billion price tag stands in sharp contrast to Hugging Face's annualised revenue of $150 million, underscoring how much of the valuation is built on strategic and growth expectations rather than current earnings.

Article Title: Iran war risk: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warns of oil shocks, sticky inflation and higher interest rates
Article Text: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has warned that the ongoing war in Iran could trigger oil and commodity price shocks, keeping inflation elevated and pushing interest rates higher than current market expectations, Reuters reported.The warning came in his annual letter to shareholders, a day after US President Donald Trump escalated pressure on Iran by threatening to target key infrastructure if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened."Now, because of the war in Iran, we additionally face the potential for significant ongoing oil and commodity price shocks, along with the reshaping of global supply chains, which may lead to stickier inflation and ultimately higher interest rates than markets currently expect," Dimon said, news agency Reuters quoted as saying.Dimon, who has led JPMorgan for two decades, also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in Ukraine, tensions in the Middle East and friction with China."The challenges we all face are significant," he added.He said it remains uncertain whether the Iran war will achieve US objectives, while warning that nuclear proliferation remains the biggest risk linked to Iran.Markets have already begun pricing in these risks, with expectations of interest rate cuts this year largely fading amid rising inflation concerns triggered by the conflict.Last week, the benchmark S&P 500 index recorded its worst quarterly performance since 2022, weighed down by rising energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty since late February.Dimon noted that the US economy remains resilient, with consumers continuing to earn and spend, and businesses staying broadly healthy, though signs of weakening have emerged.He cautioned that economic strength has been supported by significant government deficit spending and past stimulus, while infrastructure investment needs continue to grow.At the same time, he pointed to positives such as fiscal stimulus under President Trump's "Big, Beautiful Bill", deregulation policies and rising capital expenditure driven by artificial intelligence.On financial stability, Dimon said the $1.8-trillion private credit market "probably" does not pose a systemic risk, despite investor concerns and recent withdrawals from such funds.However, he warned that in a downturn, losses across leveraged lending could exceed expectations as credit standards have weakened.Private credit markets also lack transparency and rigorous valuation benchmarks, increasing the risk of investor exits if conditions worsen, he said.Separately, Dimon criticised revised US capital rules, including Basel III and GSIB surcharge norms, calling aspects of the proposals "nonsensical" and "very flawed".He said JPMorgan’s GSIB surcharge would fall only to 5.0%, a level he described as “absurd” and “un-American”, arguing it penalises the bank’s scale and performance.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warns Iran war could trigger oil and commodity price shocks. He also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in Ukraine, tensions in the Middle East and friction with China. Dimon criticised revised US capital rules, including Basel III and GSIB surcharge norms, calling aspects of the proposals "nonsensical"

Article Title: How selling Alaska in 1867 was a costly mistake for Russia
Article Text:
Image: Wikipedia

Why Russia agreed to the Alaska purchase

The hidden wealth Russia gave away

Strategic and geopolitical consequences







In 1867, Russia’s decision to sell Alaska to America turned out to be a historic mistake that was to go unnoticed for years to come. The sum paid by the US was only $7,200,000. Although, in the light of the circumstances at the time, it appeared logical, retrospectively, the act looks extremely shortsighted. Russia found itself economically constrained, geographically far away from the region and fearful of its falling into the hands of the British without any compensation. In reality, however, the region had proved immensely valuable both strategically and naturally. Its vast reserves of oil, gold, and natural resources would later transform it into one of the most economically significant territories in the United States.The choice of selling Alaska was based on economic and political reasons. By the middle of the 19th century, the Russian Empire experienced financial difficulties as a result of the expensive Crimean War. It had become increasingly hard for the country to manage such remote and thinly populated areas as Alaska.According to EBSCO , “the Russian-American Company was in decline, and the colony failed to yield any profit”.In addition to this, the lucrative fur trade had declined, making the territory much less economically valuable for the empire.At the same time, Russia was afraid that Britain might capture Alaska in case another war broke out between the two countries. Selling the colony to the friendly United States appeared as a logical step. As the Office of the Historian states, William H. However, it greatly undervalued the potential of Alaska.Another thing that Russia did not expect was the amount of riches that Alaska possessed.
